25876-the-house-with-the-green-shutters.title: The House With The Green Shutters
25876-the-house-with-the-green-shutters.creator: George Douglas
25876-the-house-with-the-green-shutters.description: A book by George Douglas. The freshness of the air, the smoke rising thin and far above the red chimneys, the sunshine glistering on the roofs and gables, the rosy clearness of everything beneath the dawn--above all, the quietness and peace--made Barbie, usually so poor to see, a very pleasant place to look down at on a summer morning.

arxiv-1904-10608.creator: Wen Huang, Zeng Lian, Xiao Ma, Leiye Xu, Yiwei Zhang
arxiv-1904-10608.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Wen Huang, Zeng Lian, Xiao Ma, Leiye Xu, Yiwei Zhang. In this article, we consider the weighted ergodic optimization problem Axiom A attractors of a C 2 C^{2} flow on a compact smooth manifold. The main result obtained in this paper is that for a generic observable from function space 𝒞 0 , α \mathcal{C}^{0,\alpha} ( α ∈ ( 0 , 1 ] \alpha\in(0,1] ) or 𝒞 1 \mathcal{C}^{1} the minimizing measure is unique and is supported on a periodic orbit.

arxiv-2110-02685.title: Particle physics in cosmic rays
arxiv-2110-02685.creator: Dariusz Góra for the Pierre Auger Collaboration
arxiv-2110-02685.description: Abstract The Pierre Auger Observatory is the world’s largest detector of ultra–high energy cosmic rays (UHECRs). It uses an array of fluorescence telescopes and particle detectors at the ground to obtain detailed measurements of the energy spectrum, mass composition and arrival directions of primary cosmic rays (above the energy of 10 17 10^{17} eV) with accuracy not attainable until now.

arxiv-2111-07791.title: On the a ​ b ​ c abc Conjecture in Algebraic Number Fields
arxiv-2111-07791.creator: Andrew Scoones
arxiv-2111-07791.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Andrew Scoones. In this paper we prove a weak form of the a ​ b ​ c abc Conjecture generalised to algebraic number fields. Given algebraic integers a , b , c a,\,b,\,c in a number field K K satisfying a + b = c a+b=c , we give an upper bound for the logarithm of the projective height H L ​ ( a , b , c ) H_{L}(a,\,b,\,c) in terms of norms of prime ideals dividing a ​ b ​ c ​

arxiv-2312-12099.title: On the structures of a monoid of triangular vector- permutation polynomials, its group of units and its induced group of permutations
arxiv-2312-12099.creator: Amr Ali Abdulkader Al-Maktry
arxiv-2312-12099.description: Abstract 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 13B25, 20B27, 16W20; Secondary 05A05, 20B25, 13M10, 14R99 Abstract Let n>1 and let R be a commutative ring with identity 1\neq 0 and R[x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}]^{n} the set of all n -tuples of polynomials of the form (f_{1},\ldots,f_{n}), where f_{1},\ldots,f_{n}\in R[x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}] . We call these n -tuples vector-polynomials.

arxiv-2401-09838.title: CATMA: Conformance Analysis Tool For Microservice Applications Conference: 2024 IEEE/ACM 46th International Conference on Software Engineering: Companion Proceedings; April 14–20, 2024; Lisbon, Portugal 2024 IEEE/ACM 46th International Conference on Software Engineering: Companion Proceedings (ICSE-
arxiv-2401-09838.creator: Clinton Cao, Simon Schneider, Nicolás E. Díaz Ferreyra, Sicco Verwer, Annibale Panichella, Riccardo Scandariato
arxiv-2401-09838.description: Abstract . The microservice architecture allows developers to divide the core functionality of their software system into multiple smaller services. However, this architectural style also makes it harder for them to debug and assess whether the system’s deployment conforms to its implementation. We present CATMA, an automated tool that detects non-conformances between the system’s deployment and implementation.

arxiv-2401-10195.title: Highly-coherent quasi-periodic oscillations in the ‘heartbeat’ black hole X-ray binary IGR J17091–3624
arxiv-2401-10195.creator: Jingyi Wang, Erin Kara, Jeroen Homan, James F. Steiner, Diego Altamirano, Tomaso Belloni ,∗ , Michiel van der Klis, Adam Ingram, Javier A. García , Guglielmo Mastroserio, Riley Connors, Matteo Lucchini, Thomas Dauser, Joseph Neilsen, Collin Lewin, Ron A. Remillard
arxiv-2401-10195.description: Abstract IGR J17091–3624 is a black hole X-ray binary (BHXB), often referred to as the ‘twin’ of GRS 1915+105 because it is the only other known BHXB that can show exotic ‘heartbeat’-like variability that is highly structured and repeated .

arxiv-2404-02386.title: Exact solution to Maxwell’s equations for the infinite ideal solenoid with a time-dependent surface current
arxiv-2404-02386.creator: Edward Parker
arxiv-2404-02386.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Edward Parker. Very little previous literature has considered the exact solution to Maxwell’s equations for an infinite ideal cylindrical solenoid with an arbitrary time-dependent azimuthal surface current K ⁡ ( t ) ​ ϕ ^ K(t)\hat{\bm{\phi}} . Most of the previous literature has focused on special cases and has approached the problem by calculating the magnetic vector potential 𝑨 \bm{A} , which requires performing some very complicated surface integrals over the cylinder.

arxiv-2407-21544.title: Temporal bandwidth of consecutive polariton condensation
arxiv-2407-21544.creator: Mikhail Misko 1,∙, Anton D. Putintsev 1,∙, Denis Sannikov 1, Anton V. Zasedatelev 1, Ullrich Scherf 2, Pavlos G. Lagoudakis 1
arxiv-2407-21544.description: Abstract The advent of organic polaritonics has led to the realisation of all-optical transistors, logic gates, and single photon-switches operating at room temperature. In this Letter, we develop a microscopic theory accounting for thermalisation, vibron-relaxation, and kinetic bimolecular quenching of polaritons and excitons to investigate the intrinsic limitations of the temporal separation of consecutive polariton condensates.

arxiv-2408-14352.title: Assessing Contamination in Large Language Models: Introducing the LogProber method
arxiv-2408-14352.creator: Nicolas Yax, Pierre-Yves Oudeyer, Stefano Palminteri
arxiv-2408-14352.description: Abstract In machine learning, “contamination” refers to situations where testing data leak into the training set. The issue is particularly relevant for the evaluation of the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs), which are generally trained on gargantuan, and generally opaque, corpora of text scraped from the world wide web.

arxiv-2412-12935.title: 𝓛 \boldsymbol{\mathcal{L}} -Lie Algebroids over Topological Ringed Spaces
arxiv-2412-12935.creator: Mainak PODDAR a and Abhishek SARKAR ab
arxiv-2412-12935.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mainak PODDAR a and Abhishek SARKAR ab. Lie algebroids over a topological ringed space provides a unified framework to study various geometric structures. This geometric concept is intimately connected with well-known algebraic structures, including Gerstenhaber algebras and Batalin–Vilkovisky algebras. We introduce more general concepts such as ℒ \mathcal{L} -Lie algebroids and 𝒜 \mathcal{A} -Gerstenhaber algebras, associated with a given Lie algebroid ℒ \mathcal{L} and Gerstenhaber algebra 𝒜 \mathcal{A} over a topological ringed space, respectively.

arxiv-2501-05541.title: Customizable LLM-Powered Chatbot for Behavioral Science Research
arxiv-2501-05541.creator: Zenon Lamprou, Yashar Moshfeghi
arxiv-2501-05541.description: Abstract . The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence has resulted in the advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) with the capacity to produce text that closely resembles human communication. These models have been seamlessly integrated into diverse applications, enabling interactive and responsive communication across multiple platforms.

arxiv-2506-15763.title: Dark Matter Surrounded Quartic Square-root Horndeski Black Hole: Thermodynamics, Optical Properties and Quasinormal Oscillations
arxiv-2506-15763.creator: Mrinnoy M. Gohain, Kalyan Bhuyan
arxiv-2506-15763.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mrinnoy M. Gohain, Kalyan Bhuyan. In this work, we study a special form of Horndeski solutions, viz. quartic "square-root" Horndeski black hole immersed in a perfect-fluid dark-matter halo, by examining its thermodynamics, null-geodesic shape, optical shadow, and quasinormal ringdown spectrum. The model is characterized by three parameters, namely β \beta , η \eta (non-minimal Horndeski coupling parameters), and b b (perfect fluid dark matter parameter), which collectively determine horizon properties and observational effects.

arxiv-2507-03592.title: Nuclear β − \beta^{-} -decay with statistical de-excitation Journal: Atomic Data and Nuclear Data Tables
arxiv-2507-03592.creator: M. R. Mumpower, T. Kawano, O. Korobkin, G. W. Misch, T. M. Sprouse
arxiv-2507-03592.description: Abstract The accurate description of nuclear β − \beta^{-} -decay has far-reaching consequences for applications spanning nuclear reactors to the creation of heavy elements in astrophysical environments. We present the nuclear particle spectra associated with the β \beta -decay of neutron-rich nuclei calculated with the well benchmarked coupled Quasi-particle Random Phase Approximation and Hauser-Feshbach (QRPA+HF) model.

arxiv-2507-19285.title: EVAluation of the Equivalent Vector Boson Approximation at highest energy colliders Preprint: DESY-25-104 COMETA-2025-29
arxiv-2507-19285.creator: Benjamin Dahlén, Maximilian Löschner, Krzysztof Mękała, Jürgen Reuter, Panagiotis Stylianou
arxiv-2507-19285.description: Abstract Collider processes at the highest available partonic center-of-mass energies – 10 TeV and above – exhibit a new regime of electroweak interactions where electroweak gauge bosons mostly act as quasi-massless partons in vector boson fusion processes. We scrutinize these processes using the Equivalent Vector boson Approximation (EVA) based on its implementation in the Monte Carlo generator framework Whizard .

arxiv-2509-22335.title: Spectral Collapse Drives Loss of Plasticity in Deep Continual Learning
arxiv-2509-22335.creator: Naicheng He, Kaicheng Guo, Arjun Prakash, Saket Tiwari
arxiv-2509-22335.description: Abstract We investigate why deep neural networks suffer from loss of plasticity in deep continual learning, failing to learn new tasks without reinitializing parameters. We show that this failure is preceded by Hessian spectral collapse at new-task initialization, where meaningful curvature directions vanish and gradient descent becomes ineffective.

arxiv-2512-12310.title: Spectrum of J P ​ C = 0 ± ⁣ ± J^{PC}=0^{\pm\pm} Gluonic Hidden-Charm Tetraquark States
arxiv-2512-12310.creator: Bing-Dong Wan 1,2 , Ming-Yang Yuan 1,2 , Jun-Hao Zhang 1,2 , and Yan Zhang 1,2
arxiv-2512-12310.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Bing-Dong Wan 1,2 , Ming-Yang Yuan 1,2 , Jun-Hao Zhang 1,2 , and Yan Zhang 1,2. We investigate gluonic hidden-charm tetraquark states composed of two valence quarks, two valence antiquarks and an explicit valence gluon.

arxiv-2602-21802.title: Non-commutative crepant resolutions for (almost) simplicial toric algebras
arxiv-2602-21802.creator: Aimeric Malter 1, Artan Sheshmani 1,2
arxiv-2602-21802.description: Abstract . Given a rational convex polyhedral Gorenstein cone constructed as cone over a lattice polytope P P , we establish that toric non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) of its associated toric algebra descend to toric NCCRs of the algebras associated to faces of the polytope P P .

pmc-10725836.creator: Xin Su, Hengqiong Gu, Fajun Li, Donglei Shi, Zhaojun Wang
pmc-10725836.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundA study aimed to estimate the burden of Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) caused by occupational exposure to particulate matter, gases, and fumes in 204 countries from 1990 to 2019.MethodsData on the deaths number, age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR), and age-standardized disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) rates (ASDR) of COPD attributable to occupational particulate matter, gases, and fumes were collected from the GBD study 2019.

pmc-11628622.title: Zonation of the Vitis vinifera microbiome in Vino Nobile di Montepulciano PDO production area
pmc-11628622.creator: Giorgia Palladino, Enrico Nanetti, Daniel Scicchitano, Nicolò Cinti, Lucia Foresto, Alice Cozzi, Antonio Gonzalez Vara Rodriguez, Nicolò Interino, Jessica Fiori, Silvia Turroni, Marco Candela, Simone Rampelli
pmc-11628622.description: The microbial dimension of the terroir is crucial for wine quality, as microbiomes contribute to plant biofertilization, stress tolerance and pathogen suppression. While microbial terroir can act as a biological signature at large scale, data for local contexts is lacking, hindering the characterization of regional microbial diversity in vineyards.

pmc-12416330.title: CPPD-related basilar impression with vertebral artery dissection and subsequent subarachnoid hemorrhage: illustrative case
pmc-12416330.creator: Sara Smeets, Thomas Daenekindt, Frank Weyns, Christophe Oosterbos
pmc-12416330.description: BACKGROUNDCalcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD) deposition disease at the craniocervical junction (CCJ) typically presents with a retro-odontoid pseudotumor. Here, the authors report a case of CPPD-induced basilar impression, causing vertebral artery (VA) dissection and hemorrhage.OBSERVATIONSA 65-year-old male presented with worsening chronic cervicalgia, occipital headaches, and unstable tandem gait.

pmc-13045043.title: Mendelian randomization and colocalization reveal potential causal effects of average daily gain on carcass composition and reproductive traits in pigs
pmc-13045043.creator: Wondossen Ayalew, Guangzhen Li, Yuqiang Liu, Jinyan Teng, Xiaodian Cai, Qing Lin, Yahui Gao, Jiaqi Li, Zhe Zhang
pmc-13045043.description: BackgroundSelective breeding has substantially improved productive and reproductive traits in pigs. Yet, these traits are biologically interconnected, and selection for one often affects others in unintended ways. While genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have uncovered many loci linked to these traits, they provide limited insight into causal mechanisms.

pmc-13310624.title: Development of chimeric antigen receptors targeting the γδ T cell receptor
pmc-13310624.creator: Lauren C Cutmore, Norris Lam, Christina Amatya, Katherine A Weissler, Stephen M Hewitt, Danielle A Natrakul, James N Kochenderfer
pmc-13310624.description: T cell malignancies expressing γδ T cell receptors (TCRs) have poor prognoses. No approved treatments specifically target γδ T cell malignancies. To address this deficiency, we aimed to develop chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) targeting the γδ TCR. We generated a panel of CARs with variations in antigen-recognition domains, hinge and transmembrane (HTM) domains, and costimulatory domains.

pmc-13330305.title: Integrating virtual patient-based learning into temporomandibular disorder education improves educational and behavioral outcomes
pmc-13330305.creator: Linda Sangalli, Elizabeth Manning, Aidai Abdykarimova, Olivia Gao, Benjamin Lok, James Hawkins, Craig S. Miller
pmc-13330305.description: BackgroundPredoctoral education in temporomandibular disorders (TMD) often provides limited opportunities for clinical exposure, which may hinder students’ competence and confidence. This study aimed to assess the educational and behavioral impact of a TMD-specific virtual patient-based learning (VPBL) intervention on dental students’ knowledge, behavioral intention for future practice, and confidence levels when integrated into a predoctoral TMD curriculum.

pmc-13414892.title: Study method for a single-arm, multi-center implementation study of strategies for use by healthcare professionals in offering smokers an adapted proactive referral for online smoking cessation treatment in health check-up settings: a hybrid type 3 effectiveness-implementation study (N-EQUITY2405)

pmc-13467249.title: Liberation from Mechanical Ventilation in Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure or Adult Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Review
pmc-13467249.creator: Karen E. A. Burns, Karen J. Bosma, Bruno L. Ferreyro, Dipayan Chaudhuri, Andrew J. E. Seely, Daniel R. Ouellette
pmc-13467249.description: Efforts to liberate patients from invasive mechanical ventilation (MV) begin when the underlying cause of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) or adult respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) that led to use of invasive ventilation has resolved or improved and patients can initiate spontaneous breaths.
